qa.q: Which plan is expressed in numerical terms and can also be used as a control device?
qa.e: Budgets state expected results in numbers and serve as standards.

qa.q: Navya Bank trains new tellers through simulated counters and role plays. The chosen way of training is a:
qa.e: A prescribed way of performing a task is a method.

qa.q: A detailed statement for launching a new hospital wing, covering objectives, staff, equipment, timeline and funds, is a:
qa.e: A programme sets out all the plans for a project.

qa.q: What is the key difference between a policy and a rule?
qa.a: A policy allows discretion while a rule allows none
qa.e: Policies are general guides; rules are rigid.

qa.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
qa.a: Procedure: chronological steps for an activity
qa.e: Only the procedure pair is correct; the others swap features of budgets, rules and policies.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Rules are the simplest type of plans. Reason (R): Rules do not allow any scope for discretion or flexibility.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Rules are simple because they just say what must or must not be done, with no discretion. R explains A.

qa.q: Organising involves identifying and grouping work, defining authority and responsibility, and:
qa.e: Organising creates working relationships among people.

qa.q: Grouping similar activities into departments is called:
qa.e: Departmentalisation forms units of similar activities.

qa.q: What is the first step of the organising process?
qa.e: First the total work is identified and divided.

qa.q: Rajan Builders allotted site work to engineers and accounts work to accountants according to their skills. Which step is this?
qa.e: Allocating jobs to suitable people is assignment of duties.

qa.q: Making clear to each employee from whom to take orders and to whom to report is:
qa.e: This creates the hierarchy of the organisation.

qa.q: Departmentalisation can be done on the basis of:
qa.e: Common bases are function, product and territory.

qa.q: Dividing work into manageable activities helps to avoid:
qa.e: Clear division means the same work is not done twice.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Assignment of duties should match jobs with the skills of employees. Reason (R): Putting the right person in the right job helps the work to be done effectively.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Matching skills to jobs leads to effective work, so R explains A.

qa.q: Systematic division of work leads to repetitive tasks and expertise. This importance is:
qa.e: Repeating a task builds skill and specialisation.

qa.q: Organising establishes clear lines of reporting. This helps in:
qa.e: Clear reporting removes confusion about who reports to whom.

qa.q: Proper assignment of work avoids duplication and wastage. This is:
qa.e: Resources are used fully without waste.

qa.q: Akash Foods added a new export department when it began selling abroad. This shows organising helps in:
qa.e: New departments let a firm grow.

qa.q: By delegating routine work, senior managers can focus on new ideas while juniors gain experience. This importance is:
qa.e: Delegation develops subordinates and frees managers for creative work.

qa.q: Clear description of jobs and authority avoids confusion and duplication, helping:
qa.e: Clarity of authority leads to effective administration.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Organising helps in adaptation to change. Reason (R): The organisation structure can be suitably modified when the environment changes.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because the structure can be revised, the firm adapts. R explains A.

qa.q: Which of these is NOT an importance of organising?
qa.a: Setting the objectives of the business
qa.e: Setting objectives is part of planning.

qa.q: Span of management refers to:
qa.a: The number of subordinates a superior can manage effectively
qa.e: Span means how many people one manager can manage effectively.

qa.q: A narrow span of management generally leads to:
qa.e: Fewer subordinates per manager means more managers and more levels.

qa.q: A factory has 72 workers and each supervisor can manage 9. How many supervisors are needed?
qa.e: Divide workers by the span.

qa.q: If the span is widened from 6 to 12 for 72 workers, how many fewer supervisors are needed?
qa.e: Span 6 needs 12 supervisors; span 12 needs 6; so 6 fewer.

qa.q: In a functional structure, activities are grouped on the basis of:
qa.a: Functions such as production, marketing and finance
qa.e: Functional structure groups jobs of similar nature by function.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of the functional structure?
qa.e: Grouping by function leads to specialisation in that function; the others are divisional advantages.

qa.q: Departments in Shree Steel focus only on their own targets and ignore company goals. This disadvantage of the functional structure is called:
qa.e: When departments care only for themselves, overall objectives suffer.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Functional structure leads to minimal duplication of effort. Reason (R): Similar activities are grouped together in one department, which brings economies of scale.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Since each function is done in one place, effort is not duplicated, so R explains A.

qa.q: A divisional structure is most suitable for a firm that:
qa.a: Produces a large variety of products using different resources
qa.e: Diverse products need separate self-contained divisions.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of the divisional structure?
qa.a: Easy to fix responsibility for each division's performance
qa.e: Each division's profit or loss shows its head's performance.

qa.q: A disadvantage of the divisional structure is:
qa.a: Increase in costs due to duplication of activities
qa.e: Each division repeats functions like marketing and finance.

qa.q: In which structure do managers get training in all functions of a product, preparing them for top positions?
qa.e: Divisional heads handle all functions for their product, which develops varied skills.

qa.q: Navtech Ltd wants to add a new solar panel line without disturbing its existing lines. Which structure helps most?
qa.e: A new division can be added easily for growth and expansion.

qa.q: Which comparison is correct?
qa.a: Functional structure is based on functions; divisional structure is based on product lines
qa.e: That is the basic difference in their formation.

qa.q: Conflict among divisional heads over the allocation of funds is a disadvantage of:
qa.e: Divisions may compete for limited resources.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Cost of operating a divisional structure is high. Reason (R): Each division has its own set of functions, leading to duplication of resources.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Repeating functions in each division raises costs. R explains A.

qa.q: Which organisation is deliberately designed by top management?
qa.e: Formal organisation is consciously created to achieve objectives.

qa.q: Informal organisation arises from:
qa.e: It emerges spontaneously from personal and social relations.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of informal organisation?
qa.a: Faster spread of information and quick feedback
qa.e: Informal channels move information quickly; the others are formal advantages.

qa.q: A disadvantage of formal organisation is that it:
qa.a: Ignores social needs and human relationships
qa.e: Formal organisation stresses work and rules, often ignoring social needs.

qa.q: In informal organisation, authority arises from:
qa.e: Informal leaders are followed because of personal qualities.

qa.q: Workers resist a new attendance system because their group decided to oppose it. Which disadvantage of informal organisation is this?
qa.e: Groups may resist change and push members to conform.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Informal organisation helps to fulfil the social needs of employees. Reason (R): Informal organisation gives employees a sense of belonging through friendships.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Belonging and friendship are social needs, so R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Formal organisation leads to faster communication than informal organisation. Reason (R): In formal organisation, communication must pass through the scalar chain.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: Passing through the scalar chain slows communication, so A is false; R is true.

qa.q: Delegation refers to:
qa.a: Downward transfer of authority from a superior to a subordinate
qa.e: Delegation passes authority down; the superior stays accountable.

qa.q: Which element of delegation cannot be delegated at all?
qa.e: Accountability stays with the superior.

qa.q: Authority flows:
qa.e: Authority flows from superior to subordinate.

qa.q: Accountability flows:
qa.e: The subordinate answers to the superior, so it flows upward.

qa.q: The obligation of a subordinate to properly perform an assigned duty is:
qa.e: Responsibility is the duty to perform; accountability is answerability for outcome.

qa.q: Ankit is told to raise sales by 20% but cannot hire staff or offer schemes. What is wrong?
qa.a: Responsibility is given without matching authority
qa.e: Authority should match responsibility for delegation to work.

qa.q: Delegation helps managers focus on important matters while subordinates handle routine work. This importance is:
qa.e: Freed time lets managers concentrate on key tasks.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A manager remains accountable even after delegating authority. Reason (R): Accountability cannot be delegated.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Since accountability cannot be passed down, the manager stays answerable. R explains A.

qa.q: Decentralisation means:
qa.a: Systematic delegation of authority to the lowest levels, except what must stay at the centre
qa.e: It spreads decision-making authority across the organisation as a policy.

qa.q: Which statement is correct?
qa.a: Delegation is compulsory, while decentralisation is optional
qa.e: Managers must delegate; decentralisation is a policy choice.

qa.q: Decentralisation develops managerial talent because:
qa.a: Lower-level managers get experience of taking decisions
qa.e: Practice in decision making prepares managers for higher posts.

qa.q: Which is the purpose of decentralisation?
qa.a: To increase the role of subordinates by giving them more autonomy
qa.e: Reducing a manager's burden is delegation's purpose; decentralisation increases subordinates' autonomy.

qa.q: Store managers at Fresh Mart decide stock levels themselves, so they respond quickly to local demand. Which importance of decentralisation is shown?
qa.e: Decisions taken at the point of action are faster.

qa.q: The scope of decentralisation, compared with delegation, is:
qa.e: Decentralisation extends to the lowest levels of the whole firm.

qa.q: Ruchi Ltd's top management is now free to focus on strategy because day-to-day decisions are taken at lower levels. This importance is:
qa.e: Freed from routine decisions, top managers can think strategically.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Centralisation and decentralisation should be balanced. Reason (R): No organisation can be completely centralised or completely decentralised.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because neither extreme works, a balance is needed. R explains A.

qa.q: Staffing is best described as:
qa.a: Filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure
qa.e: Staffing is about getting and keeping people in jobs.

qa.q: Placing the right person on the right job leads to:
qa.e: A good fit between person and job raises performance.

qa.q: Planning replacements for senior managers before they retire ensures:
qa.e: Succession planning keeps the firm running smoothly.

qa.q: Who performs the staffing function?
qa.e: Staffing is a function of every manager; HR provides specialised support.

qa.q: Which of these is an activity of HRM?
qa.a: Maintaining labour relations and handling grievances
qa.e: HRM covers people-related activities like labour relations.

qa.q: Staffing helps avoid both overmanning and shortage of staff. This is:
qa.e: Having the right number of people avoids waste and gaps.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Staffing is a function of every manager. Reason (R): Every manager has to select, train and appraise the people working under them.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Since all managers deal with their team members, staffing is everyone's function. R explains A.

qa.q: The three main aspects of staffing are:
qa.e: These are the core aspects of staffing.

qa.q: What is the first step in the staffing process?
qa.e: First the firm must know how many and what type of people it needs.

qa.q: Workload analysis helps to find:
qa.a: The number and types of people needed to perform the work
qa.e: Workload analysis estimates requirement; workforce analysis estimates availability.

qa.q: Workforce analysis reveals:
qa.a: The number and types of human resources available
qa.e: It tells what staff the firm already has.

qa.q: Introducing a selected employee to other employees and to the rules and policies of the firm is called:
qa.e: Orientation familiarises the newcomer with people and rules; placement is occupying the post.

qa.q: Evaluating an employee's actual performance against set standards is:
qa.e: Appraisal compares actual performance with standards.

qa.q: Paid leave and insurance are examples of:
qa.e: Direct pay includes wages and incentives; benefits like paid leave are indirect.

qa.q: If workload analysis shows a need for 50 people and workforce analysis shows 42 available, how many more people must be recruited?
qa.e: Requirement minus availability gives the shortfall.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Estimating manpower requirements is the first step of staffing. Reason (R): Recruitment cannot begin until the firm knows how many and what type of employees it needs.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: R explains why estimation must come first.

qa.q: Recruitment is the process of:
qa.a: Searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply
qa.e: Recruitment builds a pool of applicants; selection chooses from it.

qa.q: Which of these is an internal source of recruitment?
qa.e: Transfers and promotions are internal sources.

qa.q: Shifting an employee from one job to another without substantial change in responsibility or status is:
qa.e: A transfer is a horizontal move.

qa.q: A major limitation of internal sources is that:
qa.a: Fresh talent from outside is not brought in
qa.e: Filling posts from within limits new ideas and skills.

qa.q: Why can a newly started company not rely on internal sources?
qa.a: Because it has no existing employees to transfer or promote
qa.e: Internal sources need an existing workforce.

qa.q: Kriti, a senior executive, is made Deputy Manager with higher pay and responsibility. This is:
qa.e: Moving to a higher post with more pay is promotion.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Internal sources of recruitment motivate employees. Reason (R): Employees know they may be promoted to higher posts if they perform well.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: The chance of promotion encourages better work. R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Recruitment is a negative process. Reason (R): Recruitment encourages a large number of people to apply for jobs.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: Recruitment is positive because it attracts applicants, so A is false; R is true. Selection is the negative process.

qa.q: Which external source is most suitable for filling casual or unskilled jobs quickly at the factory site?
qa.e: A notice at the gate brings job seekers to the site.

qa.q: A database of unsolicited applications kept in the office is called:
qa.e: These are people who applied on their own without a vacancy.

qa.q: A firm wants to hire a chief technology officer with niche skills. The best source is:
qa.e: Consultants specialise in technical and managerial talent.

qa.q: Which is a merit of external sources of recruitment?
qa.e: External sources bring new skills and ideas.

qa.q: Existing employees feel unhappy when outsiders are hired for senior posts. This is a limitation of:
qa.e: Hiring from outside may cause dissatisfaction among current staff.

qa.q: Which source carries a risk of favouritism?
qa.e: Employees may recommend friends and relatives.

qa.q: Bright Minds Consulting visits management institutes to hire final-year students. This is:
qa.e: Hiring at educational institutions is campus recruitment.

qa.q: Assertion (A): External sources of recruitment can be costly. Reason (R): Firms may have to spend on advertisements and agency fees.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Advertising and agency charges raise costs. R explains A.

qa.q: Why is selection called a negative process?
qa.a: Because it rejects more candidates than it selects
qa.e: Selection eliminates unsuitable candidates.

qa.q: Which test measures an individual's potential for learning new skills?
qa.e: Aptitude means capacity to develop skills.

qa.q: A test that measures the existing knowledge and skill of a candidate in a job is:
qa.e: Trade tests check current proficiency.

qa.q: A personality test helps to assess a candidate's:
qa.e: Personality tests probe emotional and behavioural traits.

qa.q: Which step comes immediately after the employment interview?
qa.e: After the interview, references and background are verified.

qa.q: The final step of the selection process is:
qa.e: After accepting the offer, the employee signs the contract.

qa.q: Which statement about recruitment and selection is correct?
qa.e: First a pool is created, then the best are chosen.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Selection is a more complex process than recruitment. Reason (R): In selection, candidates must pass through several steps such as tests, interviews and checks.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Many steps make selection complex. R explains A.

qa.q: Training is mainly:
qa.e: Training improves skills for a specific job.

qa.q: Development is concerned with:
qa.a: Overall growth of an individual, including personality and maturity
qa.e: Development is broad and career-oriented.

qa.q: Which is a benefit of training to the organisation?
qa.e: Systematic learning reduces waste and raises output.

qa.q: Which is a benefit of training to employees?
qa.a: Better career opportunities and higher earnings
qa.e: Improved skills lead to better careers and pay.

qa.q: A new employee is introduced to colleagues, shown the workplace and told about the business on joining. This is:
qa.e: Induction helps newcomers settle in quickly.

qa.q: Increasing the knowledge and understanding of employees in a broad, conceptual way is called:
qa.e: Education builds general understanding; training is job-specific.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Training helps reduce employee turnover. Reason (R): Training increases employee morale and job satisfaction.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Satisfied employees are less likely to leave. R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Training is a wider term than development. Reason (R): Development aims at the overall growth of the individual.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: Development is wider, so A is false; R is true.

qa.q: Which is an on-the-job method of training?
qa.e: Job rotation happens at actual work places; the others are off-the-job.

qa.q: Training on dummy models of actual equipment in a separate area is:
qa.e: Vestibule training uses replicas to avoid damage.

qa.q: For jobs that require a long period of practice under a skilled master, such as plumbing, the method used is:
qa.e: Apprentices learn a trade under a master worker over time.

qa.q: Medical students working in a hospital while completing their degree is an example of:
qa.e: Internship is a joint programme of institutions and organisations.

qa.q: Information is broken into meaningful units, and the learner gets feedback after each answer. This method is:
qa.e: Programmed instruction uses small steps with rewards for correct answers.

qa.q: A manager guides a trainee and acts as his coach to prepare him as a successor. This is:
qa.e: Coaching involves a superior guiding a trainee closely.

qa.q: Metro Rail trains its train operators on a simulator before they run real trains. Why is this method preferred?
qa.a: Real equipment is costly and mistakes could be dangerous
qa.e: Vestibule-style training avoids damage and accidents on costly equipment.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Vestibule training is an off-the-job method. Reason (R): In vestibule training, employees learn on equipment similar to the actual one but away from the actual work floor.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Training away from the work floor makes it off-the-job. R explains A.

qa.q: Directing involves:
qa.a: Instructing, guiding, communicating and inspiring people
qa.e: These are the core activities of directing.

qa.q: Which characteristic of directing means it is performed at every level of management?
qa.e: Directing happens wherever there is a superior-subordinate relationship.

qa.q: Directing flows from:
qa.e: Superiors direct their subordinates.

qa.q: Which is NOT an element of directing?
qa.e: Recruitment belongs to staffing.

qa.q: Directing integrates employees' efforts because it:
qa.a: Links individual efforts towards organisational goals
qa.e: Leaders and managers align individual work with common goals.

qa.q: Plans and structures of Sagar Ltd were ready, but work began only after managers gave instructions. Which importance of directing is shown?
qa.e: Directing is the function that starts actual work.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Directing is a continuous process. Reason (R): Directing takes place throughout the life of an organisation, irrespective of people occupying managerial positions.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because it goes on throughout the organisation's life, it is continuous. R explains A.

qa.q: Through leadership, communication and motivation, directing helps balance different interests and keeps the organisation steady. This is:
qa.e: Balancing interests brings stability.

qa.q: Which principle of directing requires that individual and organisational objectives should match?
qa.e: Harmony means individual goals support organisational goals.

qa.q: Checking whether instructions given to subordinates are being implemented is the principle of:
qa.e: Follow-through means monitoring implementation.

qa.q: A manager uses employees' informal groups to spread positive information about a change. Which principle is applied?
qa.e: Effective directors use informal groups wisely.

qa.q: Supervision means:
qa.e: Supervision is watching and guiding work as it happens.

qa.q: Why is a supervisor called a 'link pin'?
qa.a: Because the supervisor links workers with management
qa.e: Supervisors convey management's ideas to workers and workers' problems to management.

qa.q: Supervisor Latha teaches a new worker how to operate the cutting machine on the shop floor. This shows the supervisor's role in:
qa.e: Supervisors train workers on the job.

qa.q: A manager chooses a motivating style for experienced staff and closer guidance for new staff. Which principle is applied?
qa.e: The technique is suited to subordinates' needs and abilities.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A supervisor helps maintain group unity among workers. Reason (R): A supervisor settles internal disputes among workers.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Settling disputes keeps the group united. R explains A.

qa.q: An inner state that energises, activates and directs behaviour towards goals is called:
qa.e: A motive is the internal force; motivators are the techniques used.

qa.q: Pay, bonus, promotion and recognition used to motivate people are called:
qa.e: These are techniques or tools of motivation.

qa.q: What comes immediately after 'unsatisfied need' in the motivation process?
qa.e: An unsatisfied need creates tension first.

qa.q: Stopping an employee's increment for poor work is an example of:
qa.e: Punishment-based motivation is negative.

qa.q: Why is motivation called a complex process?
qa.a: Because individuals differ in their needs and responses
qa.e: Different people react differently to the same motivator.

qa.q: Which is an importance of motivation?
qa.a: It reduces employee turnover and absenteeism
qa.e: Motivated employees stay longer and attend regularly.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Motivation is an internal feeling. Reason (R): Urges, drives and needs of human beings are internal, and they influence behaviour.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Motivation comes from inner needs and drives. R explains A.

qa.q: Bharat Tools offered recognition to motivated workers, and even indifferent workers became positive about their work. Which importance of motivation is shown?
qa.a: Changes negative or indifferent attitudes to positive ones
qa.e: Motivation can turn indifferent attitudes positive.

qa.q: What is the highest level in Maslow's need hierarchy?
qa.e: Self-actualisation is the top of the hierarchy.

qa.q: Job security, stability of income and pension plans satisfy which need?
qa.e: These provide economic and physical security.

qa.q: Friendship and a sense of belonging at work satisfy:
qa.e: These are social needs.

qa.q: Status, recognition and self-respect relate to:
qa.e: Esteem covers respect, status and recognition.

qa.q: Basic salary that pays for food and shelter satisfies:
qa.e: Food and shelter are basic survival needs.

qa.q: Kabir, a software engineer, has a good salary, secure job, friends and a senior title. He now wants to build an app that he believes in. According to Maslow, which need is motivating him?
qa.e: With lower needs met, he seeks to fulfil his potential.

qa.q: Which is an assumption of Maslow's theory?
qa.a: A satisfied need no longer motivates a person
qa.e: Once satisfied, a need stops motivating; the next higher one takes over.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A person moves to the next higher level of the hierarchy only when the lower need is satisfied. Reason (R): According to Maslow, human needs are arranged in a hierarchical order.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because needs are in a hierarchy, they are met from lower to higher. R explains A.

qa.q: Which of these is a financial incentive?
qa.e: Profit sharing gives employees a share in profits, a monetary reward.

qa.q: Offering shares to employees at a price lower than the market price is called:
qa.e: This makes employees part-owners at a concession.

qa.q: Designing jobs with greater variety, higher skills, more autonomy and responsibility is:
qa.e: Job enrichment makes work more challenging and meaningful.

qa.q: Car, housing, medical aid and education for children provided by an employer are:
qa.e: These are perks over and above salary.

qa.q: Giving subordinates more autonomy and powers is a non-financial incentive called:
qa.e: Empowerment means more freedom and power to act.

qa.q: Nova Textiles includes worker representatives on its canteen and safety committees. Which incentive is this?
qa.e: Involving workers in decisions through committees is participation.

qa.q: Provident fund, pension and gratuity are examples of:
qa.e: These are financial benefits given on retirement.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Non-financial incentives are important for motivating employees. Reason (R): Employees have psychological, social and emotional needs that money alone cannot satisfy.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Since money cannot meet all needs, non-financial incentives are needed. R explains A.

qa.q: Leadership is best described as:
qa.a: Influencing people to strive voluntarily towards organisational goals
qa.e: Leadership relies on influence, not force.

qa.q: A leader who centralises decisions and expects strict compliance follows the:
qa.e: Autocratic leaders command and expect obedience.

qa.q: Which style involves taking decisions in consultation with subordinates?
qa.e: Democratic leaders encourage participation.

qa.q: Dr Mehra lets his team of experienced scientists set their own work plans and only steps in when asked. His style is:
qa.e: High independence to competent subordinates marks free-rein leadership.

qa.q: Which situation best suits the autocratic style?
qa.a: When quick decisions are needed and subordinates need close supervision
qa.e: Autocratic style allows fast decisions with less consultation.

qa.q: Leadership helps resolve disagreements among team members. This importance is:
qa.e: Leaders manage conflicts effectively.

qa.q: Which is a feature of leadership?
qa.a: It shows the interpersonal relation between leader and followers
qa.e: Leadership is a relationship between leader and followers.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Democratic leadership encourages employees to participate in decision making. Reason (R): A democratic leader develops action plans and makes decisions in consultation with subordinates.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Consultation is how participation happens. R explains A.

qa.q: Communication is the process of exchanging ideas and feelings to create:
qa.e: The aim is that both sides understand the same meaning.

qa.q: Converting the message into words, symbols or gestures is called:
qa.e: Encoding happens at the sender's end.

qa.q: The receiver's response that shows the message was understood is:
qa.e: Feedback completes the communication loop.

qa.q: A poor phone connection that disturbs a conversation is an example of:
qa.e: Any obstruction in communication is noise.

qa.q: Email, letters and phone calls are examples of:
qa.e: Media is the path through which the encoded message travels.

qa.q: Which is an importance of communication?
qa.a: It acts as the basis of coordination
qa.e: Communication links departments and people, enabling coordination.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Communication promotes cooperation and industrial peace. Reason (R): Two-way communication helps management and workers understand each other.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Mutual understanding reduces conflict and builds cooperation. R explains A.

qa.q: Converting the received symbols back into meaning is done by the receiver through:
qa.e: Decoding happens at the receiver's end.

qa.q: A leave application sent by an employee to the manager is an example of:
qa.e: It goes from subordinate to superior through official channels.

qa.q: Communication between the production manager and the marketing manager is:
qa.e: It is between people at the same level in different departments.

qa.q: In which formal network does everyone communicate freely with everyone else?
qa.e: Free flow allows communication in all directions; it is fastest.

qa.q: In which formal network is communication slowest because each person talks only to neighbours?
qa.e: In a circular network, messages move slowly around the circle.

qa.q: A person who passes information only to those he or she trusts is using the:
qa.e: Cluster spreads through trusted individuals.

qa.q: Which grapevine network involves one person communicating with others at random?
qa.e: Random sharing is the probability network.

qa.q: Which is a feature of informal communication?
qa.a: It spreads fast but may distort information
qa.e: Grapevine is quick but can spread rumours.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Managers should completely ban the grapevine. Reason (R): The grapevine can be used by managers to spread useful information and get feedback from employees.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: Banning it is neither possible nor wise, so A is false; R is true.

qa.q: Which of these is a semantic barrier?
qa.e: Translation problems affect encoding and decoding of meaning.

qa.q: Judging the meaning of a message before the sender completes it is:
qa.e: Evaluating too early is a psychological barrier.

qa.q: When information passes through many levels and loses accuracy, the barrier is:
qa.a: Loss by transmission and poor retention
qa.e: Successive transfers lose part of the message.

qa.q: A status-conscious manager keeps a distance from subordinates, so they don't share problems. This is a(n):
qa.e: Status is listed among organisational barriers.

qa.q: A superior withholds information because he fears it may reduce his authority. This is a:
qa.e: Fear of challenge to authority is a personal barrier.

qa.q: The word 'value' used in 'What is the value of this ring?' and 'I value our friendship' shows the barrier of:
qa.e: One word can carry several meanings.

qa.q: Subordinates avoid sharing problems because they fear it will hurt their image. This is:
qa.e: Unwillingness to communicate is a personal barrier.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Complexity in organisation structure is a barrier to communication. Reason (R): When there are many managerial levels, communication gets delayed and distorted.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: More levels mean more filtering and delay. R explains A.

qa.q: Which measure improves communication by checking that the message has been understood?
qa.e: Feedback confirms understanding.

qa.q: Before speaking, a manager thinks through what she wants to say. Which measure is this?
qa.e: Clear thinking leads to clear messages.

qa.q: At Surya Ltd, senior employees are given the right to buy company shares at a lower price. Identify the incentive.
qa.e: Shares at a concessional price are a stock option.

qa.q: A supervisor feels a worker is lying even before he finishes his explanation, so she ignores him. Which barrier is this?
qa.e: Judging too early and distrust are psychological barriers.

qa.q: Pooja, who has a good salary, job security and friends at work, now wants recognition for her work. Which need is active?
qa.e: Recognition and status are esteem needs.

qa.q: A manager gives orders and expects them to be followed without question in an emergency. Which style is this?
qa.e: Commanding and expecting compliance is autocratic.

qa.q: Which measure suggests that a manager should check later whether the instructions given were carried out?
qa.e: Follow-up ensures action and removes hurdles.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Being a good listener improves communication. Reason (R): Patient and attentive listening solves half the problems of communication.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Listening well reduces misunderstanding. R explains A.

qa.q: Controlling means:
qa.a: Ensuring that activities are performed according to plans
qa.e: Controlling checks and corrects performance against plans.

qa.q: Controlling is called a forward-looking function because:
qa.a: It helps improve future performance by correcting deviations
qa.e: Corrective actions shape future activities.

qa.q: Close monitoring of activities at a warehouse reduced theft and dishonest behaviour. Which importance of controlling is shown?
qa.e: Controlling creates an atmosphere of order and discipline.

qa.q: Controlling reduces wastage and spoilage of resources. This is:
qa.e: Checking activities against standards cuts waste.

qa.q: Because employees know in advance the basis on which their performance will be judged, controlling helps in:
qa.e: Clear standards and fair appraisal motivate employees.

qa.q: Controlling directs all activities and efforts towards achieving organisational goals by providing a unity of direction. This importance is:
qa.e: Common standards keep all departments in step.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Controlling is a pervasive function. Reason (R): Controlling is required in all types of organisations and at all levels of management.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: R defines pervasiveness, so it explains A.

qa.q: Which statement about controlling is correct?
qa.a: It is both a backward-looking and a forward-looking function
qa.e: It reviews past performance and guides future action.

qa.q: It is difficult to measure job satisfaction and employee morale in numbers. This limitation is:
qa.e: Human behaviour is hard to quantify.

qa.q: A company cannot control a sudden change in technology or competition. Which limitation is this?
qa.e: External factors lie outside management's control.

qa.q: Employees protesting against strict monitoring shows the limitation of:
qa.e: Employees may see control as limiting their freedom.

qa.q: For a small firm, a sophisticated control system may not be justified because:
qa.e: Benefits must exceed the high cost of control.

qa.q: Which is NOT a limitation of controlling?
qa.a: It helps in judging the accuracy of standards
qa.e: Judging accuracy of standards is an importance, not a limitation.

qa.q: Kavi Motors could not meet its sales target because a new government policy raised taxes on cars. Which limitation of controlling explains this?
qa.e: Government policy is an external factor.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Controlling is less effective where standards cannot be expressed in quantitative terms. Reason (R): Without measurable standards, it is hard to compare actual performance with planned performance.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Comparison needs measurable standards; without them control weakens. R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Controlling is a cheap process for every organisation. Reason (R): Controlling involves a lot of expenditure, time and effort.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false because controlling is costly; R is true.

qa.q: What is the first step in the controlling process?
qa.e: Standards must exist before performance can be judged.

qa.q: Which of these is a qualitative standard?
qa.e: Goodwill cannot be expressed exactly in numbers.

qa.q: Personal observation, sample checking and performance reports are techniques used in:
qa.e: These methods measure what has actually been done.

qa.q: Standard sales are ₹5,00,000 and actual sales are ₹4,60,000. What is the shortfall in rupees?
qa.e: Shortfall = standard − actual.

qa.q: In the same case (standard ₹5,00,000, actual ₹4,60,000), what is the percentage shortfall?
qa.e: Divide the shortfall by the standard, not by the actual.

qa.q: Why should actual performance be measured in the same units as the standard?
qa.a: So that a meaningful comparison can be made
qa.e: Comparison is only possible in the same units.

qa.q: Comparing actual performance with standards reveals:
qa.a: Deviations between actual and desired results
qa.e: Comparison shows gaps, which are deviations.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Standards should be flexible. Reason (R): Standards may need to be modified when there are changes in the business environment.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Since conditions change, standards must be adjustable. R explains A.

qa.q: 'An attempt to control everything results in controlling nothing.' This is the basis of:
qa.e: Only significant deviations should reach management.

qa.q: Focusing control on key result areas that are critical to success is:
qa.e: KRAs are the critical points.

qa.q: Planned material cost is ₹200 per unit with a permissible deviation of 5%. Actual cost is ₹206. What is the percentage deviation?
qa.e: Divide the deviation by the planned cost.

qa.q: In the same case, the 3% deviation should be:
qa.a: Ignored, as it is within the permissible 5%
qa.e: Under management by exception, deviations within limits need no attention.

qa.q: Output fell because machines are outdated. What corrective action is suitable?
qa.e: Obsolete machinery needs a technology upgrade.

qa.q: A plant finds defects are due to poor quality raw material. The corrective action is:
qa.a: Change the quality specifications for materials used
qa.e: Defective material calls for revised material specifications.

qa.q: Which step of controlling is this? 'The manager finds out why sales fell short of target in the eastern region.'
qa.e: Finding causes of a gap is analysis of deviations.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Under critical point control, a small increase in a key cost may need more attention than a large increase in a minor cost. Reason (R): Key result areas are critical to the success of the organisation.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because KRAs affect success, even small deviations there matter more. R explains A.

qa.q: Planning and controlling are called:
qa.e: They depend on each other completely.

qa.q: 'Controlling without planning is blind' because:
qa.a: Without plans there are no standards to control against
qa.e: Plans provide the standards for comparison.

qa.q: Planning is __________ whereas controlling is __________.
qa.e: Planning prescribes; controlling evaluates.

qa.q: How is planning backward-looking?
qa.a: It is guided by past experiences and results of earlier control
qa.e: Planning draws on past performance revealed by controlling.

qa.q: How is controlling forward-looking?
qa.a: Its corrective action improves future performance
qa.e: Corrections guide future activities.

qa.q: Which statement best describes the relationship?
qa.a: Planning is a prerequisite for controlling, and controlling completes planning
qa.e: Plans come first; controlling checks and closes the loop.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Planning without controlling is meaningless. Reason (R): Once a plan is implemented, controlling is needed to monitor progress and correct deviations.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Without checking, plans may go off track unnoticed. R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Planning is only forward-looking and controlling is only backward-looking. Reason (R): Planning and controlling are both backward-looking as well as forward-looking.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false because both functions look in both directions; R is true.

qa.q: Financial management is concerned with:
qa.a: Optimal procurement as well as usage of finance
qa.e: It covers both raising and using funds efficiently.

qa.q: The primary objective of financial management is:
qa.e: Shareholders' wealth, shown by the share price, is the key objective.

qa.q: Wealth of shareholders is measured by the:
qa.e: A higher market price means more wealth for shareholders.

qa.q: Which is a role of financial management?
qa.a: Deciding the proportion of debt and equity in long-term finance
qa.e: Capital structure is a core financial decision.

qa.q: Business finance refers to:
qa.a: The money required for carrying out business activities
qa.e: It is all funds needed by the business.

qa.q: Deciding how much to keep in cash, inventory and receivables is part of determining the:
qa.a: Quantum and break-up of current assets
qa.e: Current assets include cash, inventory and receivables.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A financial decision is good if it increases the market value of equity shares. Reason (R): Wealth maximisation of shareholders is the main objective of financial management.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because the objective is shareholders' wealth, decisions that raise share value are good. R explains A.

qa.q: Financial management also affects items in the profit and loss account because:
qa.a: Choices of financing and investment change interest, expenses and depreciation
qa.e: Debt brings interest; assets bring depreciation.

qa.q: Capital budgeting decisions relate to investment in:
qa.e: Capital budgeting is about long-term investment in fixed assets.

qa.q: Which is NOT a factor affecting capital budgeting decisions?
qa.e: Shareholder preference affects dividend decisions.

qa.q: Why are capital budgeting decisions important?
qa.a: They involve large funds and are irreversible
qa.e: Large, long-term, hard-to-reverse commitments make them critical.

qa.q: Decisions about investment in current assets like inventory and receivables are called:
qa.e: Short-term investment decisions concern working capital.

qa.q: Two projects have the same cost, but one generates higher cash inflows over its life. Which factor favours it?
qa.e: Higher expected cash inflows make a project more attractive.

qa.q: Sun Agro decides to buy a new cold storage plant worth ₹15 crore. This is a(n):
qa.e: Buying a fixed asset is a capital budgeting decision.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Capital budgeting decisions affect the long-term growth of a firm. Reason (R): These decisions affect the earning capacity of the business over the long run.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Earning capacity over many years drives growth. R explains A.

qa.q: An investment decision with a wrong choice of a ₹50 crore plant cannot be easily undone. This shows capital budgeting decisions are:
qa.e: Reversing such decisions involves heavy loss.

qa.q: Financing decision is concerned with:
qa.a: The amount of funds to be raised from various long-term sources
qa.e: It decides the mix of sources like debt and equity.

qa.q: Debt is considered cheaper than equity mainly because:
qa.a: Interest on debt is a tax-deductible expense
qa.e: Tax deduction lowers the effective cost of debt.

qa.q: If the promoters of a company do not want to lose control, they will prefer:
qa.e: Debt holders do not get voting rights, so control is not diluted.

qa.q: A company with a strong and stable cash flow position can safely use:
qa.e: Strong cash flows make it easy to pay interest and repayments.

qa.q: During a stock market boom, companies find it easier to raise:
qa.e: Investors are keen to buy shares in a boom.

qa.q: Which source of finance has no floatation cost?
qa.e: Retained earnings are generated internally, so there is no issue cost.

qa.q: A firm with high fixed operating costs (rent, insurance, salaries) should:
qa.e: High fixed operating costs plus fixed interest raise risk.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Debt is a riskier source of finance for a company than equity. Reason (R): Payment of interest and repayment of principal on debt are obligatory.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Fixed obligations create risk of default. R explains A.

qa.q: The dividend decision is concerned with:
qa.a: How much profit to distribute and how much to retain
qa.e: It splits profit between dividends and retained earnings.

qa.q: A company with many growth opportunities is likely to:
qa.a: Pay lower dividends and retain more
qa.e: Retained earnings fund growth.

qa.q: A loan agreement says the company cannot pay a dividend above 10% until the loan is repaid. Which factor is this?
qa.e: Conditions in loan agreements are contractual constraints.

qa.q: Companies try to keep dividend per share steady and change it only when earning potential has truly gone up. This factor is:
qa.e: Firms prefer a stable dividend pattern.

qa.q: An increase in dividend is generally taken as a positive signal by investors. This factor is:
qa.e: Share prices tend to react positively to higher dividends.

qa.q: Which of these is a dividend decision?
qa.a: Deciding to retain 60% of profit for expansion
qa.e: Retention vs distribution of profit is a dividend decision.

qa.q: Zeta Ltd's profits are high, but most of it is stuck with debtors. Which factor may limit its dividend?
qa.e: Dividends are paid in cash; low cash limits payout.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Companies with good growth opportunities retain more money out of their earnings. Reason (R): Retained earnings can be used to finance the investment needed for growth.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Retaining profit provides the funds for growth, so R explains A.

qa.q: Financial planning is essentially:
qa.a: Preparation of a financial blueprint of future operations
qa.e: It plans future funds and their uses.

qa.q: One objective of financial planning is to:
qa.a: Ensure availability of funds whenever required
qa.e: Funds must be available at the right time.

qa.q: Why should a firm avoid raising more funds than required?
qa.a: Excess funds add to cost and may encourage wasteful spending
qa.e: Idle funds cost money and may be wasted.

qa.q: Financial planning helps a business face sudden changes like a fall in sales without panic. This importance is:
qa.a: Helps avoid business shocks and surprises
qa.e: Forecasting prepares the firm for surprises.

qa.q: Financial planning helps coordinate which functions?
qa.a: Sales, production and other business functions
qa.e: It aligns funds with the needs of all functions.

qa.q: Long-term financial plans usually cover a period of:
qa.e: Long-term plans span 3 to 5 years; short-term budgets one year or less.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Financial planning makes evaluation of actual performance easier. Reason (R): It provides detailed plans against which actual results can be compared.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: A plan gives the benchmark for comparison. R explains A.

qa.q: By estimating fund requirements and their sources together, financial planning:
qa.e: It shows how planned investments will be financed.

qa.q: Capital structure refers to the mix of:
qa.e: It is about how the firm is financed: debt and equity.

qa.q: Trading on equity is favourable when:
qa.a: Return on investment is higher than the cost of debt
qa.e: Then debt earns more than it costs, raising EPS.

qa.q: A company has debt of ₹40 lakh and equity of ₹80 lakh. What is its debt-equity ratio?
qa.e: Debt ÷ Equity = 40 ÷ 80.

qa.q: Total funds ₹20 lakh; EBIT ₹3 lakh; debt ₹15 lakh at 10%; equity ₹5 lakh in shares of ₹10; tax 30%. What is the EPS?
qa.e: Subtract interest, then tax, and divide by the number of shares.

qa.q: Total funds ₹20 lakh (all equity, shares of ₹10); EBIT ₹1,60,000; tax 30%. What is the EPS?
qa.e: No interest; deduct tax and divide by 2,00,000 shares.

qa.q: Same firm (total funds ₹20 lakh, EBIT ₹1,60,000, tax 30%) now uses ₹10 lakh debt at 10% and ₹10 lakh equity in shares of ₹10. What is the EPS?
qa.e: ROI is 8%, below the 10% interest, so debt lowers EPS.

qa.q: In the case above, ROI is 8% and the cost of debt is 10%. What happens to EPS as more debt is used?
qa.e: When ROI < cost of debt, each rupee of debt costs more than it earns.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Trading on equity is favourable when the return on investment is higher than the rate of interest on debt. Reason (R): In that case, the surplus earned on borrowed funds over their interest cost goes to the equity shareholders, raising EPS.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: The extra earning on debt beyond its cost increases equity earnings, which is exactly why trading on equity is favourable. R explains A.

qa.q: Interest coverage ratio is calculated as:
qa.e: It shows how many times EBIT covers interest.

qa.q: A company's EBIT is ₹18 lakh and its interest charge is ₹6 lakh. What is its interest coverage ratio?
qa.e: Divide EBIT by interest.

qa.q: Firm P has ICR 6 and Firm Q has ICR 1.5. Which is in a better position to raise more debt?
qa.e: Higher ICR means more cushion to pay interest.

qa.q: A higher tax rate makes debt:
qa.a: Relatively cheaper, because interest is tax-deductible
qa.e: Tax savings on interest lower the after-tax cost of debt.

qa.q: Keeping some borrowing capacity unused so that the firm can borrow in future emergencies is the factor of:
qa.e: Flexibility preserves future borrowing power.

qa.q: A firm with high business risk should generally:
qa.e: High business risk plus high financial risk would be dangerous.

qa.q: As a firm uses more and more debt, equity shareholders expect a higher return. This factor is:
qa.e: Higher financial risk raises the return shareholders demand.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A company with a higher debt service coverage ratio can include more debt in its capital structure. Reason (R): A higher DSCR indicates a better ability of the company to meet its cash commitments for servicing debt.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Better ability to service debt makes more borrowing safe, so R explains A.

qa.q: Fixed capital refers to investment in:
qa.a: Long-term assets like land, buildings and machinery
qa.e: Fixed assets are held for long-term use.

qa.q: Which business generally needs the least fixed capital?
qa.e: Trading needs few fixed assets compared to manufacturing.

qa.q: A firm that chooses a capital-intensive technique will need:
qa.e: Machines and automation need heavy investment.

qa.q: Leasing machinery instead of buying it reduces fixed capital needs. This factor is:
qa.e: Leasing is an alternative way to finance asset use.

qa.q: In industries where assets become obsolete quickly, fixed capital requirement is:
qa.e: Frequent replacement needs more fixed capital.

qa.q: Nova Foods plans to start a new dairy line alongside its biscuits. Its fixed capital needs will rise because of:
qa.e: Entering new product lines needs new assets.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Fixed capital decisions involve a high degree of risk. Reason (R): They involve large funds committed for a long period, and future returns are uncertain.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Large, long-term commitments under uncertainty create risk. R explains A.

qa.q: A larger scale of operations generally needs:
qa.e: Bigger operations need more plant and machinery.

qa.q: Net working capital is calculated as:
qa.e: Net working capital is the excess of current assets over current liabilities.

qa.q: Current assets are ₹72 lakh and current liabilities are ₹48 lakh. What is the net working capital?
qa.e: Subtract current liabilities from current assets.

qa.q: A business with a longer production cycle needs:
qa.e: Funds remain blocked in work-in-progress for longer.

qa.q: If suppliers give a firm generous credit, its working capital requirement:
qa.e: Credit availed means less cash is needed upfront.

qa.q: A firm that allows customers long credit periods needs:
qa.e: Cash is blocked in receivables.

qa.q: During a boom, the working capital requirement generally:
qa.e: Higher sales and production need more current assets.

qa.q: A restaurant needs less working capital than a car manufacturer mainly because of:
qa.e: Service and trading firms carry less inventory and get cash quickly.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Higher inflation increases the working capital requirement. Reason (R): Rising prices increase the cost of raw materials and labour.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: More money is needed to keep the same level of operations. R explains A.

qa.q: A financial market is a market for:
qa.a: Creation and exchange of financial assets
qa.e: Financial markets deal in financial assets.

qa.q: The allocative function of a financial market means:
qa.a: Channelling savings into the most productive investment uses
qa.e: It allocates funds from savers to investors.

qa.q: The money market deals with funds having a maturity of:
qa.e: It is the market for short-term funds.

qa.q: Which of these is a major participant in the money market?
qa.e: RBI, banks and large institutions dominate the money market.

qa.q: Which pair links the two sides of a financial market?
qa.e: Households save; businesses invest.

qa.q: Which is NOT a participant in the money market?
qa.a: An individual buying a single share of ₹100 on the stock exchange
qa.e: Buying a share is a capital market activity; money market deals are large and short-term.

qa.q: Assertion (A): The money market is a market for short-term funds. Reason (R): It deals in monetary assets with a maturity period of up to one year.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: R gives the time limit that makes it short-term. R explains A.

qa.q: Through which two routes can savings reach investors?
qa.a: Through banks or directly through financial markets
qa.e: Funds can flow via banks or financial markets.

qa.q: The capital market deals in:
qa.e: It provides medium and long-term finance.

qa.q: Which market offers higher safety to investors?
qa.e: Short duration and sound issuers make money market instruments safer.

qa.q: Which market generally gives higher expected returns?
qa.e: Higher risk in the capital market brings higher expected returns.

qa.q: Which is TRUE about investment outlay?
qa.a: Capital market investment can be small, while money market deals need huge sums
qa.e: Shares have small unit values; money market instruments are expensive.

qa.q: Equity shares, debentures and bonds are instruments of the:
qa.e: These are long-term securities.

qa.q: Which is a component of the capital market?
qa.e: Development banks, commercial banks and stock exchanges make up the capital market.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Capital market securities are considered liquid. Reason (R): They can be bought and sold on stock exchanges.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Trading on stock exchanges allows quick conversion to cash. R explains A.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Money market instruments are riskier than capital market instruments. Reason (R): Money market instruments have a short duration and are issued by financially sound institutions.
qa.a: A is false, but R is true
qa.e: A is false: money market instruments are safer. R is true and is the reason they are safer.

qa.q: The primary market is also known as the:
qa.e: It deals with securities issued for the first time.

qa.q: Which market provides liquidity to existing securities?
qa.e: Investors can sell existing securities on the stock exchange.

qa.q: In which market do both buyers and sellers happen to be investors?
qa.e: Existing securities are traded among investors.

qa.q: Which market contributes directly to capital formation?
qa.e: Funds raised go directly to the company for investment.

qa.q: Prices of securities in the secondary market are determined by:
qa.e: Market forces set secondary market prices.

qa.q: Which market has no fixed geographical location?
qa.e: New issues can be made anywhere; the secondary market operates through stock exchanges.

qa.q: Kunal buys shares of an already-listed company on the stock exchange. This transaction takes place in the:
qa.e: Buying existing shares is a secondary market deal.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Only listed securities can be traded in the secondary market. Reason (R): Securities of a company issued for the first time need not be listed to be offered in the primary market.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Both statements are true, but R is about the primary market and does not explain the listing rule of the secondary market.

qa.q: A stock exchange is defined under which Act?
qa.e: The SCRA 1956 defines a stock exchange.

qa.q: In which year was the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act passed?
qa.e: It is the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956.

qa.q: Prices of securities on a stock exchange are determined by:
qa.e: Interaction of buyers and sellers sets prices.

qa.q: Encouraging people to invest in ownership securities through education and wider participation is called:
qa.e: Equity cult means popularising investment in shares.

qa.q: Why is the stock exchange called an economic barometer?
qa.a: Because stock indices reflect the state of the economy
qa.e: Market indices move with economic conditions.

qa.q: Investors trust trading on a stock exchange because dealings take place within a well-regulated legal framework. This function is:
qa.e: Regulation makes transactions safe.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A stock exchange contributes to economic growth. Reason (R): Through the process of disinvestment and reinvestment, savings get channelled into their most productive investment avenues.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Channelling savings into productive investment drives growth. R explains A.

qa.q: Which is the correct pair?
qa.e: Sensex is the BSE index; Nifty belongs to the NSE.

qa.q: What is the first step in trading securities on a stock exchange?
qa.e: Only registered brokers can trade on the exchange.

qa.q: A contract note is issued by the broker within:
qa.e: The broker issues the contract note within 24 hours of the trade.

qa.q: Holding securities in electronic form instead of paper certificates is called:
qa.e: Demat means converting paper securities to electronic form.

qa.q: Which are the two depositories in India?
qa.e: NSDL and CDSL hold securities in electronic form.

qa.q: Under T+1 settlement, a trade done on Wednesday is normally settled on (assuming no holidays):
qa.e: T+1 means one working day after the trade day.

qa.q: Who acts as an agent of the depository and deals directly with investors?
qa.e: DPs like banks and brokers open and maintain demat accounts.

qa.q: Which is a benefit of dematerialisation?
qa.a: It removes the risk of theft, loss and forgery of share certificates
qa.e: Electronic holding avoids problems of paper certificates.

qa.q: Assertion (A): A demat account is needed to trade in shares on a stock exchange. Reason (R): Shares bought and sold on stock exchanges are held and transferred in electronic form.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because shares move electronically, an electronic account is needed. R explains A.

qa.q: SEBI was given statutory status in the year:
qa.e: SEBI was set up in 1988 and became statutory in 1992.

qa.q: SEBI was first set up as an interim administrative body in:
qa.e: It was established on 12 April 1988.

qa.q: Controlling insider trading is a ________ function of SEBI.
qa.e: Insider trading harms investors; controlling it protects them.

qa.q: Training of intermediaries in the securities market is a ________ function of SEBI.
qa.e: Developing skills of intermediaries develops the market.

qa.q: Registration of brokers, sub-brokers and merchant bankers is a ________ function of SEBI.
qa.e: Registering intermediaries is regulation.

qa.q: Which was a reason for setting up SEBI?
qa.a: Malpractices such as price rigging and delays in delivery of shares
qa.e: Malpractices in the growing capital market led to SEBI's creation.

qa.q: SEBI publishes research on market trends and allows internet trading through registered brokers. These are examples of its:
qa.e: Research and flexible market development are developmental.

qa.q: Assertion (A): One objective of SEBI is to protect the rights and interests of investors. Reason (R): SEBI guides and educates investors and prohibits fraudulent and unfair trade practices.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Education and prohibition of fraud are how SEBI protects investors. R explains A.

qa.q: In the modern sense, a market refers to:
qa.a: The set of actual and potential buyers of a product
qa.e: Modern marketing sees the market as buyers, not a place.

qa.q: Who is a marketer?
qa.a: The person or firm that organises the exchange process
qa.e: Usually the seller who arranges exchange is the marketer.

qa.q: Which is a feature of marketing?
qa.e: A market offering details the product's size, quality, price and availability.

qa.q: Customer value means:
qa.a: The benefits a customer gets are greater than the cost paid
qa.e: Buyers judge value by benefits versus cost.

qa.q: A campaign urging people to donate blood is marketing a(n):
qa.e: Social causes are ideas.

qa.q: Advertising flats in a new housing project is marketing:
qa.e: Real estate is property.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Marketing involves an exchange mechanism. Reason (R): Marketing involves exchange of products and services for money or something of value.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Exchange is at the core of marketing. R explains A.

qa.q: According to the modern concept, the main focus of marketing is:
qa.a: Satisfying the needs and wants of customers
qa.e: Modern marketing starts from customer needs.

qa.q: Selling focuses on:
qa.a: Transfer of ownership of goods from seller to buyer
qa.e: Selling aims to complete the exchange.

qa.q: Which statement about selling and marketing is correct?
qa.a: Selling is a part of marketing
qa.e: Marketing is wider and includes selling.

qa.q: Marketing begins:
qa.a: Before production, by identifying customer needs
qa.e: Marketing starts by finding out what customers want.

qa.q: The strategy used in selling is mainly:
qa.e: Selling pushes the existing product.

qa.q: Marketing management is the art and science of choosing target markets and:
qa.a: Getting, keeping and growing customers through superior customer value
qa.e: This is the essence of marketing management.

qa.q: Marketing emphasises:
qa.e: Customer needs are the starting point.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Marketing continues even after the sale is completed. Reason (R): Marketing aims at long-term customer satisfaction through after-sale service and feedback.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Long-term satisfaction needs after-sale effort. R explains A.

qa.q: Planning, organising, directing and controlling activities that facilitate exchange is called:
qa.e: These management functions applied to marketing make marketing management.

qa.q: Under the production concept, profit is earned mainly through:
qa.e: Mass production and wide distribution at low cost drive profit.

qa.q: Which concept says customers will prefer products with the best quality, performance and features?
qa.e: The product concept focuses on product improvement.

qa.q: Which concept relies on aggressive selling and promotion?
qa.e: It assumes customers won't buy enough unless persuaded.

qa.q: The starting point of the marketing concept is:
qa.e: Marketing concept begins with identifying customer needs.

qa.q: Which concept adds society's long-term well-being to customer satisfaction?
qa.e: Societal marketing balances customer, company and society.

qa.q: Sudha Mills keeps costs low by producing in huge quantities and selling through many outlets. Which concept is it following?
qa.e: Availability and affordability through mass production is the production concept.

qa.q: A phone maker adds feature after feature without checking what buyers want. Which concept is this?
qa.e: Focus on product features and quality is the product concept.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Under the societal marketing concept, a firm should avoid products that harm society, even if customers want them. Reason (R): The societal marketing concept considers the long-term well-being of society along with customer needs.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Because society's welfare matters, harmful products should be avoided. R explains A.

qa.q: Producing goods according to predetermined specifications is called:
qa.e: Standardisation ensures uniform quality.

qa.q: Classifying products into different groups on the basis of quality or size is:
qa.e: Grading sorts products by features.

qa.q: Storing goods until they are needed by customers is the function of:
qa.e: Warehousing creates time utility.

qa.q: After-sales service, handling complaints and credit facilities are part of:
qa.e: These keep customers satisfied after the sale.

qa.q: A company surveys young buyers to learn what features they want in a scooter. This function is:
qa.e: Research into needs is market information.

qa.q: Which is a role of marketing in the economy?
qa.a: It creates demand that supports production and employment
qa.e: Marketing links producers and consumers and drives demand.

qa.q: Moving goods from the factory to retailers by road and rail is the function of:
qa.e: Transportation moves goods to where they are needed.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Grading helps in selling agricultural products. Reason (R): Grading classifies products into groups with similar quality, so buyers can choose easily.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Clear quality groups build buyer confidence. R explains A.

qa.q: The 4Ps of the marketing mix are:
qa.e: These are the four elements of the marketing mix.

qa.q: A product is described as a bundle of:
qa.e: It offers functional, psychological and social utilities.

qa.q: Products bought frequently, immediately and with minimum effort are:
qa.e: Little effort is needed to buy them.

qa.q: Products bought after comparing quality, price and style are:
qa.e: Buyers compare before buying.

qa.q: For which type of product do buyers make a special purchase effort due to unique features?
qa.e: Unique products justify extra effort.

qa.q: Tyres bought by a car manufacturer are:
qa.e: They become part of the final product.

qa.q: A factory building and heavy machinery are classified as:
qa.e: Installations are long-lasting capital items.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Stationery and lubricants used by a business are industrial supplies. Reason (R): Supplies are short-lived items that help in the operations of a business.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: They are consumed in running the business, so they are supplies. R explains A.

qa.q: The part of a brand that can be spoken is the:
qa.e: A brand name is verbal; a brand mark is visual.

qa.q: A brand or part of a brand that is given legal protection is a:
qa.e: Registration gives exclusive legal rights.

qa.q: Which is an advantage of branding to customers?
qa.e: Customers can spot and trust a brand quickly; the others benefit marketers.

qa.q: The immediate container of a product, like a toothpaste tube, is the:
qa.e: It holds the product directly.

qa.q: Packaging has become important due to self-service outlets because:
qa.a: The package must attract and inform buyers without a salesperson
qa.e: In self-service stores, the pack does the selling.

qa.q: A label that shows the statutory warning on a cigarette pack performs which function?
qa.e: Laws require certain information on labels.

qa.q: Which is a characteristic of a good brand name?
qa.a: Short, easy to pronounce and remember
qa.e: Simple, distinctive and protectable names work best.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Branding allows a firm to charge a price higher than competitors. Reason (R): A brand creates differentiation and customers may pay more for a trusted brand.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Differentiation and trust allow premium pricing. R explains A.

qa.q: Price is defined as:
qa.a: The amount of money paid by buyers in consideration of the purchase
qa.e: It is what the buyer pays for the product.

qa.q: Which factor sets the minimum price of a product?
qa.e: A firm must recover its costs.

qa.q: The upper limit of a product's price is set by:
qa.e: Buyers will not pay more than the utility they get.

qa.q: When there is very little competition, a firm can generally:
qa.e: Less competition means more pricing freedom.

qa.q: A company prices its premium phone very high to signal top quality. Which objective is it pursuing?
qa.e: High price can signal and support quality leadership.

qa.q: Fixed, variable and semi-variable costs together make up the:
qa.e: All costs together give total cost.

qa.q: A firm that offers free home delivery and long credit may need to charge a higher price. Which factor is this?
qa.e: Customer services and credit add to costs and shape price.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Governments may regulate the prices of essential commodities. Reason (R): Price regulation helps protect consumers from unfair high prices.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Consumer protection is the reason for price control. R explains A.

qa.q: Selling through company-owned outlets directly to customers is a:
qa.e: No middlemen means zero level.

qa.q: Manufacturer → Retailer → Customer is a:
qa.e: There is one middleman, the retailer.

qa.q: How many middlemen are there in a three level channel?
qa.e: Agent, wholesaler and retailer.

qa.q: Perishable products like fresh fish generally need:
qa.e: Quick movement avoids spoilage.

qa.q: Which is a component of physical distribution?
qa.e: Physical distribution covers order processing, transport, warehousing and inventory control.

qa.q: A company with strong finances and a wish for tight control over sales may prefer:
qa.e: Financial strength allows direct distribution with more control.

qa.q: Maintaining a large stock of goods to ensure a continuous flow of supply is the channel function of:
qa.e: Accumulation means holding large stocks so that supply continues smoothly.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Industrial products generally use direct or short channels. Reason (R): Industrial products are often technical, made to order and bought in large quantities by a few buyers.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Few large buyers and technical needs make direct selling practical. R explains A.

qa.q: Which are the tools of the promotion mix?
qa.a: Advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and public relations
qa.e: These are the four promotional tools.

qa.q: Which feature makes advertising impersonal?
qa.a: There is no direct face-to-face contact with each buyer
qa.e: Advertising speaks to many people at once through media.

qa.q: Which is a limitation of advertising?
qa.e: It is hard to know immediately how the audience responded.

qa.q: Critics say advertising adds to cost. The usual answer is that:
qa.a: Advertising increases demand, leading to economies of scale and lower cost per unit
qa.e: Larger volumes spread costs over more units.

qa.q: Which is a feature of personal selling?
qa.a: It develops a personal relationship with the customer
qa.e: Face-to-face contact builds relationships.

qa.q: Which tool is more flexible, allowing the message to be adjusted to each customer?
qa.e: Salespeople adapt to the buyer's reactions.

qa.q: Personal selling helps society by:
qa.a: Converting latent demand and creating employment
qa.e: It turns hidden demand into sales and offers careers.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Cost of reaching each person is lower in advertising than in personal selling. Reason (R): Advertising reaches a large number of people at the same time through mass media.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Spreading cost over a huge audience lowers cost per person. R explains A.

qa.q: Sales promotion refers to:
qa.e: It boosts sales quickly through offers.

qa.q: 'Buy a shirt and get a tie free' is an example of:
qa.e: A different product is given free with the purchase.

qa.q: Offering a product at a reduced price to clear excess stock is called:
qa.e: A rebate is a special price cut to clear stock.

qa.q: A limitation of sales promotion is that it:
qa.a: May spoil the image of the product
qa.e: Too many offers make buyers doubt quality.

qa.q: Public relations mainly aims to:
qa.a: Build and maintain a favourable image and goodwill
qa.e: PR manages the company's reputation.

qa.q: A company holds a press conference to clear a false rumour about its product. This is:
qa.e: Handling rumours through media is a PR activity.

qa.q: Which promotional tool is shown? 'A salesperson visits offices to demonstrate a new photocopier.'
qa.e: Face-to-face demonstration is personal selling.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Sales promotion is useful when a new product is launched. Reason (R): Incentives like samples and introductory discounts encourage people to try the new product.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Trial offers break buyers' hesitation. R explains A.

qa.q: Consumer protection includes:
qa.a: Educating consumers and providing redressal for their complaints
qa.e: It covers awareness and remedies.

qa.q: Many buyers do not know their rights or how to complain. This reason for consumer protection is:
qa.e: Lack of awareness makes consumers easy to exploit.

qa.q: Consumers are scattered and weak compared with large sellers. This is called:
qa.e: Without organisation, consumers have little bargaining power.

qa.q: A business that ignores consumers may face stricter control by the government. This reason is:
qa.e: Self-regulation helps avoid government action.

qa.q: Since business uses resources like land, water and people from society, it should protect consumers. This reason is:
qa.e: Using society's resources creates a duty to serve society.

qa.q: Adulteration, false weights and misleading claims are signs of:
qa.e: These unfair practices exploit consumers.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Consumer protection is in the long-term interest of business. Reason (R): Satisfied customers lead to repeat sales and good word of mouth.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: Repeat sales and goodwill help business last. R explains A.

qa.q: 'It is the duty of business to act honestly and avoid exploiting customers.' This reason is:
qa.e: Doing the right thing is a moral reason.

qa.q: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the Consumer Protection Act of:
qa.e: The 1986 Act was replaced by the 2019 Act.

qa.q: Under the Act, who is NOT a consumer?
qa.a: A person who buys goods for resale
qa.e: Buying for resale or commercial purpose is excluded.

qa.q: Which transactions are covered by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
qa.e: The Act covers e-commerce, teleshopping, direct selling and more.

qa.q: Ravi buys an auto-rickshaw and drives it himself to earn his livelihood. Under the Act, he is:
qa.a: A consumer, as self-employment for livelihood is not a commercial purpose
qa.e: The Act excludes self-employment for livelihood from 'commercial purpose'.

qa.q: A patient treated totally free of charge at a charitable camp is, under the Act:
qa.a: Not a consumer, as no consideration was paid
qa.e: Consideration is needed to be a consumer of services.

qa.q: Which is an objective of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?
qa.a: To set up authorities for timely and effective settlement of consumer disputes
qa.e: It protects consumer interests and provides quick redressal.

qa.q: Assertion (A): Asha's brother, who uses the scooter she bought with her approval, is a consumer under the Act. Reason (R): The definition of consumer includes any user of goods with the approval of the buyer.
qa.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
qa.e: R gives the exact rule that makes the brother a consumer. R explains A.

qa.q: Goods bought on deferred payment (instalments) are covered because the definition of consumer includes consideration that is:
qa.a: Paid, promised, partly paid or under any system of deferred payment
qa.e: Any form of consideration counts.

qa.q: A consumer was injured by a pressure cooker that burst due to a defect. Which right was violated?
qa.e: Protection against hazardous goods is the right to safety.

qa.q: A packet of biscuits has no information about ingredients or expiry date. Which right is violated?
qa.e: Consumers must know quality, quantity, purity and price.

qa.q: Which mark should a consumer look for when buying gold jewellery?
